scope: web/bike/*.js (Bluetooth, Zwift, FIT encoding, workouts, metrics)
Architecture: file-based (JSON), no database, no backend APIs

vulnerabilities.description: Protobuf varint decoder lacks buffer bounds checking.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Malformed Zwift Ride controller message with truncated varint → bytes[i++] after i >= bytes.length returns undefined → (undefined & 0x7f) evaluates to NaN → infinite loop or arithmetic overflow in varint accumulation.

vulnerabilities.description: Protobuf length-delimited field loop reads past buffer without bounds validation.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Message with length-delimited field (tag wire=2) claiming end > bytes.length → while (i < groupEnd) or while (i < end) increments i past allocated buffer → out-of-bounds memory read; potential information disclosure or crash.

cleared.note: No API keys, passwords, or tokens hardcoded in source files. .env.example contains placeholders. Secrets loaded from environment only (~/.config/paceforge/env, sessionStorage).
No SQL queries. File-based storage (JSON via Pydantic). Not vulnerable.

User-controlled content escaped via escHtml() before rendering (CLAUDE.md: 'XSS protection via escHtml() utility for all user-controlled content in templates'). XML entity decoder used only for workout numeric parsing, not user-facing strings.
File operations protected: is_relative_to() + resolve() in backend. Tarfile exports use filter=data. Web Bluetooth and fetch() origin-scoped.

Session auth via httpOnly cookies (cookie-session) + scrypt hash (n=2¹⁴/r=8/p=1). Garmin login interactive (getpass, no terminal echo). OAuth tokens ephemeral and refreshed per sync. Upload credentials in sessionStorage only (never persisted to disk).
Python backend: fixed argument lists (subprocess.run, shell=False). No string interpolation. Instance name validated via regex before systemd/Caddy use.
urllib3 emscripten worker buffers pre-allocated by caller. Web modules first-party. No untrusted npm.

recommendations: Add bounds check to varint decoder (line 34): if (i >= bytes.length) throw new Error('varint: unexpected EOF at byte ' + i)
Add bounds check to length-delimited field reader (line 51): if (end > bytes.length) throw new Error('protobuf field length overflows buffer')
Fuzz protobuf decoder with truncated/malformed Zwift Ride messages to verify bounds checks
Document Zwift Ride protocol as experimental/reverse-engineered in code comments
attestations: No SQL injection vectors (file-based, no queries).
XSS mitigated by escHtml() on all user-facing content.
Path traversal protected via is_relative_to() + resolve().
Authentication uses scrypt hashes and httpOnly cookies.
Subprocess invocations use fixed argument lists (shell=False).
Secrets stored in environment or sessionStorage only, never persisted to disk or localStorage.
notes: File-based architecture (data/*.json) eliminates entire classes of backend vulnerabilities (SQL injection, NoSQL injection, database escapes).
Multi-user isolation via OS-level directory + port separation, not app-level tenancy. No cross-athlete data leakage possible.

Zwift Ride controller is reverse-engineered protocol (sources: makinolo.com, ajchellew/zwiftplay). Protobuf implementation is minimal hand-rolled decoder, not production-grade. Varint and length-delimited field handling should be hardened.
Garmin login uses Cloudflare WARP socks5 proxy (PF_GARMIN_PROXY) to bypass per-IP rate limits. WARP security is not under app control.
Upload tokens (intervals.icu, Strava) in sessionStorage (ephemeral, cleared on browser exit), never disk-backed. Transmitted over HTTPS via Authorization header.
Bike profile (FTP, power history) stored in localStorage with NS namespace suffix to isolate multiple portal instances in one browser.
